idea.en: Isolate a hepatic vein through the liver.

steps.en: What you see: A hepatic vein runs toward the cava with a clean Doppler gate position clear of the trunk. Normal flow steps forward twice per beat, the systolic step taller than the diastolic.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values and regurgitation thresholds: Systolic flow reversal in the hepatic vein marks severe tricuspid regurgitation.
Severe tricuspid regurgitation means vena contracta 7 mm or more with effective orifice 0.40 sq cm or more.
Normal hepatic flow is systolic dominant with forward flow in both systole and diastole.

Pitfalls: Atrial fibrillation removes the atrial kick and blunts the pattern, so compare with the ECG. In constriction the diastolic wave dominates with expiratory reversal; do not confuse this with regurgitation.

spot.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Portal vein mistaken for hepatic vein, portal flow is phasic toward the liver. Correct it by checking direction with colour, since hepatic flow runs toward the cava.
Sampling the cava instead of the vein. Correct it by moving the gate into the branch until the trace sharpens.
Respiratory drift moving the gate out of the vessel. Correct it by asking for a held breath out and repositioning before recording.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at subcostal right, sagittal oblique through the liver toward the cava.
Point the probe marker toward the head, about twelve o clock.
Angle obliquely through the liver until one vein runs straight toward the cava. Keep the gate small and clear of the cava mouth to avoid contamination.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Use systolic reversal as a severe tricuspid regurgitation clue.

q.en: Normal hepatic vein Doppler looks like what?

why.en: Health shows forward flow twice per beat with systole taller.

q.en: Systolic reversal appears in the hepatic vein. What does this mark?

why.en: Systolic reversal is a specific marker of severe tricuspid regurgitation.

q.en: How do you separate hepatic from portal vein?

o.en: Hepatic flow runs toward the cava while portal flow runs toward the liver

why.en: Direction with colour decides: hepatic drains out, portal flows in.
